raw_response:
Ai, let me think through this year. Same as always, really — wheat and maize on the same little 4 mu plot, been doing it 40 years.

My old man passed a while back and the kids are in the city, send me a bit of money each month. So I'm alone on the plot. Can't swing a hoe like when I was young — for plowing I hire old Liu's tractor, and the big combine comes through the village at wheat harvest. Costs some money but there's no other way.

**Wheat** — I planted last October, around National Day time. Got my seed from the shop in town, the regular kind everyone uses, about 40 yuan's worth per mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — two bags for my plot. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up, so I'll top-dress with urea when I irrigate, maybe a bag and a half. My neighbor Wang's daughter-in-law uses more but their plot is bigger. I do what I've always done — works out to maybe 16 kg of nitrogen per mu all told, that's what the extension fellow said years back and I stuck with it.

Water — the well costs money every time I turn on the pump. I did one before winter, one at green-up, one more at jointing. Three times. If it stays dry at grain-fill I'll do a fourth, but usually three is enough. Electricity adds up.

The aphids come at heading, so I spray once. And a herbicide in early spring. That's all.

I expect about 400 kg per mu. That's what I usually get.

**Maize** — goes in right after wheat comes off in June. Tight, maybe three or four days between. No time to plow properly — I just have the seed drilled right into the stubble, everyone does it now. Hybrid seed from the shop, costs a bit but you can't save maize seed, doesn't work. Put compound fertilizer down with the planter. If the plants look pale in July I'll top-dress once more.

Rain is usually enough for maize here in summer, but last year was dry so I irrigated twice. I'll see. About 450 kg per mu is what I aim for.

That's the year.
